extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners implementing the cross-entropy (CE) method for stochastic/combinatorial optimization (e.g., max-cut, TSP)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying and implementing the Cross-Entropy (CE) method to (discrete and continuous) multi-extremal optimization problems, including sample generation, parameter updating, smoothing, stopping, and adaptive (FACE) variants, with concrete examples (max-cut, TSP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required algorithm inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The stopping criterion, the initial vector ˆv0, the sample size N and the number ρ have to be specified in advance, but the rest of the algorithm is 'self-tuning'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four items must be set before running Algorithm 2.3; other aspects (e.g., reference parameter updates) are determined by the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping criterion (quantile stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop if for some t ≥ d we have ˆγt = ˆγt−1 = · · · = ˆγt−d (equation (34)); denote the final iteration by T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: d is chosen in advance (examples use d=3 or d=5). This detects convergence of the (1−ρ)-quantile estimate across d iterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoothed updating (smoothing parameter α)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of replacing ˆvt−1 by ˆw t directly use ˆvt = α ˆw t + (1 − α) ˆvt−1 (equation (35)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smoothing prevents entries reaching 0 or 1 permanently. Empirically α between 0.4 and 0.9 gives best results; α = 1 recovers the original update (no smoothing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 0/1 entries in parameter vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrences of 0s and 1s in the parameter vectors are undesirable because once an entry is 0 or 1 it often will remain so forever, which is undesirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use smoothing (see previous item) especially for discrete random variables to keep parameters away from exact 0 or 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two essential ingredients to apply CE
rubrics_metrics.description: For each problem one must (1) specify how the samples are generated (the family of pdfs { f(·; v) }), and (2) calculate the updating rules for the parameters, based on cross-entropy minimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many ways to generate samples exist; choice affects performance and tractability of updating formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter updates via MLE on elite samples
rubrics_metrics.description: ˆvt is equal to the MLE based only on the sample vectors xi for which performance S(xi) ≥ ˆγt (connection between CE update (33) and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement updating by maximizing the (weighted) log-likelihood over the elite subset. In examples this yields closed-form updates (e.g., Bernoulli case (36)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size selection relative to number of parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose sample size N proportional to the number of ASP parameters to estimate: for an SNN-type problem N = c n (n = number of nodes), for SEN-type N = c n^2 (n^2 = number of edges); generally to estimate k parameters take N = c k with c > 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical constant choices: 5 ≤ c ≤ 10 for SNN; choose c>1; ensure enough samples to reliably estimate parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of rarity parameter ρ
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines: take ρ around 0.01 provided n is reasonably large (n ≥ 100); for n < 100 take a larger ρ, e.g. ρ ≈ ln(n)/n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ρ controls the (1−ρ)-quantile used to define elite samples; choose according to problem size and parameter dimensionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative performance (weighting) functions ϕ(s;γ)=ψ(s)I{s≥γ}
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the indicator I{s≥γ} by ϕ(s;γ)=ψ(s)I{s≥γ} with ψ(s) increasing to favor higher-performing samples more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical evidence suggests ψ(s)=s can speed up convergence; avoid high-power polynomials ψ(s)=s^β with large β and Boltzmann ψ(s)=e^{−s/β}, which may lead to local minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACE: use elite-count N_elite to adapt N and ρ
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Fully Adaptive CE (FACE) algorithm adapt sample size Nt and rarity implicitly by fixing the number of elite samples N_elite; ρt = N_elite/Nt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended N_elite = c0 n for SNN and N_elite = c0 n^2 for SEN, where c0 typically in [0.01,0.1]. Replace fixed (N,ρ) by (Nt, N_elite) and adapt Nt between N_min and N_max each iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACE sampling plan and improvement checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the sampling plan so with high probability S*_{t} > S*_{t−1} (best elite performance improves). Use two improvement checks: (53) S*_{t} > S*_{t−1} and (54) ˆγt > ˆγt−1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start each iteration with N_min samples and increase Nt if improvement checks are violated, up to N_max. If checks hold, perform parameter updating using the N_elite best samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACE stopping rules and 'hard' problem detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop if the best elite sample S* has not changed over the last d iterations (S*_{t} = ··· = S*_{t−d}); if Nt reaches N_max and improvement checks persistently fail for c iterations (e.g., c=3), stop and declare a 'hard' problem with an unreliable estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical choices: N_min = n, N_max = 20 n for SNN; c default = 3; this procedure flags pathological cases where CE can no longer improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Max-cut sampling and updating (Bernoulli model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate cuts by independent Bernoulli variables X2,...,Xn with success probabilities p2,...,pn (x1 fixed=1). Update p_j via p̂_{t,j} = sum_{i} I{S(X_i)≥γ̂_t} I{X_{i,j}=1} / sum_{i} I{S(X_i)≥γ̂_t} (equation (39)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the MLE on elite samples for the Bernoulli family; extend to r-partitions by using independent r-point distributions instead of Bernoulli.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSP sampling via Markov chain and transition-matrix updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent tours as permutations; generate random tours using a Markov chain with transition matrix P (diagonal elements 0). Update p_{i j} by the fraction of transitions from i to j among elite tours (equations (48)/(49)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice use Algorithm 3.1 to generate valid tours (zero-out the visited column and normalize rows) to avoid generating irrelevant paths. The update has the natural interpretation: pi j = (count of i→j in elite tours)/(count of i-occurrences in elite tours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialization guidance for reference parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose sensible initial ˆv0 appropriate for the problem (examples: for max-cut use p0 = (1, 1/2, ..., 1/2); for TSP take ˆP0 with all off-diagonal elements 1/(n−1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good initialization helps convergence; stopping criterion still uses quantile-stability (34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example/default CE parameter settings (practical recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical example choices used in experiments: rarity parameter ρ = 0.1 or 0.01, smoothing α = 0.7 (or α=1 for no smoothing), stopping constant d = 3 or d = 5, sample size N = 10 n^2 (for some TSP examples) or N = 1000 (max-cut synthetic example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical observations: decreasing N from 10 n^2 to 5 n^2 increases relative experimental error by at most a factor of 1.5 in reported case studies; adjust parameters by problem size and desired accuracy/CPU budget.
